\begin{theorem}[Expectation deviation and nonconstant Fourier mass]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sub_mean_le_fourierOneNorm_sub}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b004
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sub_mean_le_fourierOneNorm_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsFourierRegular, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.isBiased_iff_isFourierRegular, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.covariance, FABL.covariance_eq_sum_fourierCoeff_mul, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.mean}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that is $\varepsilon$-biased,
and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The absolute difference between the $\phi$-weighted
expectation of $f$ after identifying the Boolean cube with the sign cube, and the
uniform mean of $f$, is at most $\bigl(\|\widehat f\|_1-|\widehat
f(\varnothing)|\bigr)\varepsilon$, where $\|\widehat f\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute
Fourier coefficients and $\widehat f(\varnothing)$ is the constant Fourier coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm of a product]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_pointwise_mul_le}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_pointwise_mul_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_pointwise_mul, FABL.fourierOneNorm}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and all real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, the Fourier one-norm of their pointwise product is at most
the product of their Fourier one-norms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm of a square]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_sq_le}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.fourierOneNorm_pointwise_mul_le}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The Fourier
one-norm of the pointwise square of $f$ is at most the square of the Fourier one-norm of
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared expectation deviation bound]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sq_sub_mean_sq_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b006
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sq_sub_mean_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sub_mean_le_fourierOneNorm_mul, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.fourierOneNorm_sq_le, FABL.mean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that is $\varepsilon$-biased for
some $\varepsilon\geq0$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The absolute difference
between the $\phi$-weighted expectation of $f^2$ after identifying the Boolean cube with
the sign cube, and the uniform mean of $f^2$ on the sign cube, is at most $\|\widehat
f\|_1^2\varepsilon$, where $\|\widehat f\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of the
Fourier coefficients of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Refined squared expectation deviation bound]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sq_sub_mean_sq_le_refined}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b006
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sq_sub_mean_sq_le_refined}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.abs_expectation_signFunction_sub_mean_le_fourierOneNorm_sub, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.fourierOneNorm_sq_le, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that is $\varepsilon$-biased for
some $\varepsilon\geq0$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The absolute difference
between the $\phi$-weighted expectation of $f^2$ after identifying the Boolean cube with
the sign cube, and the uniform mean of $f^2$ on the sign cube, is at most
$\bigl(\|\widehat f\|_1^2-\|f\|_2^2\bigr)\varepsilon$, where $\|\widehat f\|_1$ is the
sum of the absolute Fourier coefficients and $\|f\|_2$ is the uniform $L^2$ norm.
\end{theorem}
